newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - LSWR drops, swaps undermine fuel.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - LSWR drops, swaps undermine fuel.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil closed weaker Monday on lower crude values and renewed physical selling by a major with no buying support seen, traders said.
The weaker market was also attributed to large falls to swap prices where the front month March swaps was sold down sharply in active trade.
March swaps was last quoted at $99.50/$100.50 per tonne, down from Friday's $102.50/$103.00 per tonne.
The market was traded down throughout the day at $101.00, $100.75 and $100.50 per tonne. Late day it traded several times at $100.00, brokers said.
Traders said the sell pressure came from players looking to lock in a East/West spread by selling the Med and buying the East at around $6.00 per tonne.
In the physical market, a European major offered 20,000 tonnes loading March 22-26 at $101.50 per tonne free-on-board Singapore but no buyers emerged.

Traders said the weaker physical market was also due to reduced spot purchases from China which covered most of its requirements for up to first half delivery from South Korea. Despite the lower exports to China, exports to the region are unchanged with some MidEast sellers even looking to ship
additional cargoes to the region.
Low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) moved down under aggressive trader selling, offering on a fixed price at $18.75 per barrel fob for March barrels.
A Japanese trader emerged to bid at $17.50 and bought the 100,000-barrel cargo at $18.25 fob Singapore/Indonesia lifting March 11-15.
The buyer said on a floating basis, he would bid 20 cents per barrel over Pertamina's formula with offers were heard from 50-70 cents.
Some traders said prices had room to come down further in line with the drop in crude and good supplies, but expected $17.00 to be the floor.
But other traders were not as bearish saying the U.S. refiner who had been offering a 600,000-barrel cargo for late February, was not in the market any longer.
A Japanese trader was heard seeking 100,000 barrels for mid-March lifting.

Regional demand for March is currently assessed just over 3 million barrels; 1.2 million to Japan, 0.5 million to South Korea, 560,000 to Italy, 400,000 to India and over 400,000 barrels to Australia.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
